name: Gnathosaurus
sum: Spoonbill-like ctenochasmatid from the Late Jurassic of Bavaria (and possibly the Purbeck of England); first mistaken for a crocodile.
wsnote: About 1.7 m for the 1951 adult skull.
holotype: Jaw fragment named Crocodilus multidens (1832), Solnhofen limestone; later G. subulatus.
material: Skulls and jaws only (28 cm adult skull with up to 130 teeth); G. macrurus from a partial lower jaw and neck vertebrae.
exceptional: Bennett (2025) argued that juvenile skeletons named Aurorazhdarcho micronyx belong to this species.
biology: Needle-like teeth around a spoon-shaped tip: probably waded with open jaws and snapped them shut on small prey, like modern spoonbills.
author: Meyer 1833
